# Lift bridge native surface candidates

## Scope

Direct binary32 positions from all five native main render meshes, at all three LODs. The installed native decompressor reads mesh 0; its indices are compared exactly with the prior bone-group OBJ export. Extra meshes, separate pillars and footings are not classified here.

Candidate selection is offline: upward triangles with all three Y values exactly equal, grouped by bone and Y, ranked by projected area. This excludes sloped surfaces and is not a road-removal mask or a runtime classifier. Bone -1 denotes mixed-bone triangles.

## Required follow-through

Review geometry, material/UV ownership, vertical edges and fixed/moving interfaces before producing any runtime mask or seam table. Near geometry defines logical ownership; a far proxy must not redefine the road datum. Full triangle membership for the twenty largest groups per mesh is retained in the intermediate extraction. No generated bridge or runtime behavior was inspected. No runtime code, native resources, installed payload or bridge assets changed.

## Observations that change the replacement plan

Lift03 has large moving-bone-3 candidates at both Y=19.7998046875 and
Y=9.800048828125 in the near/middle meshes. They must remain separate inputs when
reviewing the measured main/auxiliary arrangement; a single road-height mask would lose
one layer. Far geometry uses different proxy levels and does not redefine traffic height.

Lift01 near/middle has a large bone-4 candidate at Y=9.800048828125. Its far mesh does
not contain the corresponding large exactly-horizontal candidate at that datum. The
largest horizontal far-mesh group is instead high fixed structure at Y=80.578125.
This rules out choosing the largest horizontal group as the road or assuming a flat
near-road plane exists unchanged at every LOD. Sloped and composite proxy faces require
inspection beyond this exact-horizontal candidate instrument.

Lift02 near/middle candidates include multiple distinct moving levels around the road
rather than one common exact height. Lift04 and Lift05 also have sizeable structural
candidates on their moving bone. Bone identity plus area alone cannot classify road faces.
The next step is semantic/UV and boundary review per style and LOD, retaining original
structural channels/topology. No candidate has been promoted to a runtime deletion mask.
